args.query:
// Countries: high-frequency JOINT_DRIVER_WITH edges at p90 threshold (~>=19)
MATCH (a:Substance)-[r:JOINT_DRIVER_WITH]-(b:Substance)
WHERE r.frequency >= 19
MATCH (a)-[:IS_DRIVER]->(site:Site)<-[:IS_DRIVER]-(b)
WHERE site.country IS NOT NULL
WITH DISTINCT id(r) AS edge_id, site.country AS country
WITH country, count(DISTINCT edge_id) AS highfreq_edges
// driver and site coverage per country
MATCH (drv:Substance)-[:IS_DRIVER]->(s2:Site)
WHERE s2.country = country
WITH country, highfreq_edges, count(DISTINCT drv) AS n_drivers, count(DISTINCT s2) AS n_sites
WITH country, n_sites, n_drivers, highfreq_edges,
     CASE WHEN n_drivers>1 THEN toFloat(highfreq_edges) / (toFloat(n_drivers) * (n_drivers - 1) / 2.0) ELSE null END AS density_pairwise,
     CASE WHEN n_drivers>0 THEN toFloat(highfreq_edges) / toFloat(n_drivers) ELSE null END AS edges_per_driver
RETURN country, n_sites, n_drivers, highfreq_edges, round(edges_per_driver,3) AS edges_per_driver, round(density_pairwise,5) AS density_pairwise
ORDER BY highfreq_edges DESC
LIMIT 30

Yes. Using the JOINT_DRIVER_WITH edge frequency to represent how often two substances co-occur as mixture risk drivers, the network is denser in some countries and river basins than others.

How I defined “high-frequency” and “density”
- High-frequency co-driver edges: r.frequency ≥ 19 (top 10% of all JOINT_DRIVER_WITH edges; p90 ≈ 18.9 across 992 edges).
- Density (pairwise): highfreq_edges divided by the number of possible driver pairs, n_drivers × (n_drivers − 1) / 2.
- I also report edges_per_driver: highfreq_edges / n_drivers.
- To avoid inflated densities from tiny basins, I show two basin views: all basins (for absolute edges) and basins with n_drivers ≥ 30 (for more robust densities).

Observed patterns
- Countries (p90 threshold):
  - By density (pairwise): Sweden 0.00839; Germany 0.00294; Slovakia 0.00230; Netherlands 0.00108; France 0.00061.
  - By absolute high-frequency edges: Netherlands 34; Sweden 12; Germany 10; France 10; Slovakia 1.
  - Interpretation: Sweden has the densest high-frequency co-driver network among countries with ≥50 drivers, while the Netherlands has the most high-frequency edges in absolute terms but lower density due to a large driver set.

- River basins (p90 threshold):
  - By absolute edges (top basins): Rijn 31 (density 0.00166); “NA” 23 (0.00209); Meuse 15 (0.00182); Schelde 12 (0.00444); Loire Bretagne 7 (0.00123).
  - Densest among well-covered basins (n_drivers ≥ 30): Eems 0.00581; Schelde 0.00444; Artois Picardie 0.00366; “NA” 0.00209; Meuse 0.00182.
  - Note: Several very small basins (1 site, a handful of drivers) show artificially high densities; the n_drivers ≥ 30 filter reduces this bias.

What this means (interpretation grounded in the data)
- Countries: The high-frequency co-driver network is most concentrated in Sweden when controlling for the number of drivers; the Netherlands concentrates the largest number of such edges overall but with lower relative density.
- Basins: Among well-sampled basins, Eems and Schelde show the densest high-frequency co-driver structure; Rijn has many high-frequency edges in absolute terms but a lower relative density.

Reproduce these results
- Frequency distribution (to set the p90 threshold):
  MATCH (:Substance)-[r:JOINT_DRIVER_WITH]-(:Substance)
  RETURN count(r) AS edges,
         min(r.frequency) AS minf,
         percentileCont(r.frequency, 0.5) AS p50,
         percentileCont(r.frequency, 0.75) AS p75,
         percentileCont(r.frequency, 0.9) AS p90,
         percentileCont(r.frequency, 0.95) AS p95,
         max(r.frequency) AS maxf,
         avg(r.frequency) AS avgf

- Countries (p90 threshold, density and edges per driver):
  MATCH (a:Substance)-[r:JOINT_DRIVER_WITH]-(b:Substance)
  WHERE r.frequency >= 19
  MATCH (a)-[:IS_DRIVER]->(site:Site)<-[:IS_DRIVER]-(b)

  WITH DISTINCT id(r) AS edge_id, site.country AS country
  WITH country, count(DISTINCT edge_id) AS highfreq_edges
  MATCH (drv:Substance)-[:IS_DRIVER]->(s2:Site)
  WHERE s2.country = country
  WITH country, highfreq_edges, count(DISTINCT drv) AS n_drivers, count(DISTINCT s2) AS n_sites
  WITH country, n_sites, n_drivers, highfreq_edges,
       CASE WHEN n_drivers > 1 THEN toFloat(highfreq_edges) / (toFloat(n_drivers) * (n_drivers - 1) / 2.0) ELSE null END AS density_pairwise,
       CASE WHEN n_drivers > 0 THEN toFloat(highfreq_edges) / toFloat(n_drivers) ELSE null END AS edges_per_driver
  RETURN country, n_sites, n_drivers, highfreq_edges,
         round(edges_per_driver, 3) AS edges_per_driver,
